Package com.oracle.database.selectai.agent

Interface SelectAIAgent

All Superinterfaces:
AutoCloseable
public interface SelectAIAgent extends AutoCloseable
Client interface for Oracle Select AI Agent operations.

This interface provides access to the agent framework resources managed by DBMS_CLOUD_AI_AGENT: agents, tasks, tools, and teams. It also provides collection-level operations for listing agents, tasks, tools, and teams, executing teams, inspecting and updating team state, accessing runtime variables, retrieving object definitions, and importing team definitions.

Use SelectAIAgent separately from SelectAI so agent orchestration and application-facing Select AI profile operations remain explicit. Agent resources may use Select AI profiles, but creating or managing an agent resource does not create or modify a profile.

SelectAIAgent extends AutoCloseable. Creating a client with create(DbConnectionConfig) opens one SDK-owned JDBC connection immediately. Call close() when the client is no longer needed to release that connection and its database session.

Creating a client with create(DataSource) does not obtain a connection immediately. The application owns the DataSource; the SDK borrows a connection for each database operation and closes that connection after use, returning pooled connections to their pool. Calling close() does not close the caller-owned DataSource. Each operation may therefore use a different pooled connection; applications should not depend on uncommitted transaction or other session state being available to a later operation.

The name-only agent(String), task(String), tool(String), and team(String) factories verify that the current user owns the resources and load their metadata and attributes before returning. Granted cross-schema teams can be run through runTeam(String, RunTeamRequest) without loading owner-only metadata. The owner-scoped list methods also load metadata and attributes for each returned handle. listAvailableTeams() provides a separate read-only discovery view backed by DBMS_CLOUD_AI_AGENT.LIST_TEAMS; its results may include shared teams that cannot be opened with team(String). The overloads that accept attributes retain their configuration without a database query; a resource is not persisted until its create() method succeeds. For agents, required attribute values such as profile name and role are validated by the database during Agent.create(), not by the AgentAttributes builder.

For a complete runnable example, see CreateAgentSample source. For an end-to-end example that creates a tool, task, agent, and team, runs the team, and continues the same conversation, see AgentWorkflowSample source.

Since:
1.1.0

    • runTeam

      TeamRunResult runTeam(String teamName, RunTeamRequest request) throws SelectAIException
      Runs an existing team by name without loading owner-only team metadata. A consumer can run a team granted by another database user with a name such as TEAM_OWNER.SHARED_SUPPORT_TEAM. The database checks team existence and the caller's access; this method does not grant access to manage the team's definition. Without established session context, the request must contain a database-created conversation identifier. The operation is synchronous. In DataSource mode, the borrowed JDBC connection can remain occupied for the duration of the workflow. The SDK does not provide a cancellation API, and a JDBC timeout or interrupted call may not stop server-side or provider work. Retry only when the workflow is known to be safe to repeat.

      For a runnable example, see RunSharedTeamSample source.

      For a human-input workflow resumed in a new process through a pooled DataSource, see PooledTeamResumeSample source.

      Parameters:
      teamName - team name, optionally owner-qualified
      request - prompt and optional runtime parameters
      Returns:
      typed team-run result retaining the database response
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - when teamName is null or blank, or request is null
      SelectAIException - when the database rejects or cannot complete the run

    • getTeamStateByConversationId

      TeamExecutionState getTeamStateByConversationId(String teamName, String conversationId) throws SelectAIException
      Returns the latest state for a team run identified by a database conversation identifier.

      This operation does not load a Team handle and supports an owner-qualified team name for a shared team.

      For a runnable example, see GetTeamStateSample source. For a runnable example that verifies WAITING_FOR_HUMAN before resuming through a pooled DataSource, see PooledTeamResumeSample source.

      Parameters:
      teamName - team name, optionally owner-qualified
      conversationId - existing database conversation identifier
      Returns:
      typed team execution state retaining the original database value
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - when either argument is null or blank
      SelectAIException - when the database operation fails
      Since:
      1.1.0

    • grantTeamAccess

      boolean grantTeamAccess(String teamName, String userOrRoleName) throws SelectAIException
      Grants a database user or role permission to run an owner-managed team. The connected database user must own the team, and teamName must be the owner's unqualified team name. This method does not load a Team handle and is useful when the owner wants a client-level sharing operation.

      For a runnable example, see GrantTeamAccessSample source.

      Parameters:
      teamName - owner's unqualified team name
      userOrRoleName - database user or role receiving execution access
      Returns:
      true when the database accepts the grant
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - when either name is null, blank, invalid, or the grantee is PUBLIC
      SelectAIException - when the database rejects or cannot complete the grant
      Since:
      1.1.0

    • getVariable

      default String getVariable(String namespace, String name) throws SelectAIException
      Reads an ephemeral runtime variable from the current database session.

      Runtime variables are session-scoped. In DataSource mode, separate calls may use different pooled connections, so applications that require the value to remain available across calls should use a connection mode that retains one database session or manage the session explicitly.

      For a runnable example, see GetVariableSample source.

      Parameters:
      namespace - runtime-variable namespace, such as state_variables
      name - runtime-variable key
      Returns:
      the variable value, or null when the key is not set
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - when namespace or name is null or blank
      SelectAIException - when the database operation fails
      Since:
      1.1.0
